Marubeni Corporation.desc: A Japanese general trading and investment company, founded in 1858 and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, dealing in food and agriculture, metals and minerals, energy and chemicals, power and infrastructure, finance and leasing, and aerospace. The group had 52,658 employees as of 31 March 2026.

HP Gauff Ingenieure.desc: A German engineering and consulting firm in Nuremberg, founded in 1988, that plans and manages water, sewage, energy, road, traffic and airport projects, mainly in Germany, Europe and Africa; it now trades as GAUFF GmbH & Co. Engineering KG. About 70 staff work at the Nuremberg head office.

sources.title: GAUFF GmbH & Co. Engineering KG company record
sources.publisher: Bayern International / Key to Bavaria (Bavarian state business database)

Ondeo (Suez).desc: Ondeo was the water arm of the French utility group Suez, created as a single brand in March 2001 to hold Lyonnaise des Eaux, Nalco and Degremont; at launch it reported revenues of 9.1 billion euros and 60,000 staff in 130 countries. Suez, listed on Euronext Paris and the New York Stock Exchange, had group revenues of 39.6 billion euros in 2003 and sold Ondeo Nalco that year; the Ondeo brand was later dropped.

Benpres (Lopez group).desc: A Philippine investment holding company incorporated in 1993 for the Lopez family, holding stakes in broadcasting, telecoms, power and banking; at the end of 2009 it held 57 percent of ABS-CBN Broadcasting and 42 percent of First Philippine Holdings. It was renamed Lopez Holdings Corporation in 2010.

sources.title: SEC okays Benpres name change to Lopez Holdings

Vivendi.desc: A French group that began as a water company and became a media and telecoms business; it merged with Seagram and Canal Plus in December 2000 to form Vivendi Universal, with shares on Euronext Paris and the New York Stock Exchange. Revenues were 25.5 billion euros in 2003; it sold down its environmental arm, renamed Veolia Environnement in 2003.

sources.title: Vivendi Universal Form 20-F for fiscal year 2003

Anglian Water (AWG Group).desc: Anglian Water Services supplies water and runs sewerage networks for nearly seven million customers in eastern England; it is the main operating company of Anglian Water Group, registered in Jersey and tax resident in the UK. AWG was a London-listed group until investors bought it in 2006 and took it private.

Sociedad Comercial del Plata (Soldati gr.desc: An Argentine holding company founded in 1927, the main vehicle of the Soldati family's business group, with stakes in building materials, fuel distribution, food, oil and gas, and rail freight. Its shares trade on the Buenos Aires stock exchange in the MerVal index, and group sales were about 476 million US dollars in 2025.

Motor Columbus (LAMI consortium).desc: A Swiss electricity holding company based in Baden, listed on the SWX Swiss Exchange, whose main asset was a 58.5 percent stake in the power company Atel; its shareholders at the end of 2005 were UBS (55.6 percent), EDF International (20 percent) and EOS Holding (15.5 percent). Group net sales were 8.58 billion Swiss francs with about 8,377 staff in 2005; it was merged into Atel in 2006 and the name disappeared.

Acres International.desc: An employee-owned Canadian consulting engineering firm in Oakville, Ontario, with about 800 staff, working on power, water resources and oil and gas projects. It agreed to be bought by the engineering group Hatch in July 2004 and was renamed Hatch Acres in 2005.

LTA Ltd..desc: A South African building, civil and mechanical engineering contractor, formed in 1965 from the merger of James Thompson, Lewis Construction, Steeledale Reinforcing and Amco, and listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. It later became part of the Aveng group and traded as Aveng Grinaker-LTA.

Campenon Bernard.desc: A French civil engineering and construction firm founded in 1920 by Edme Campenon and Andre Bernard, building bridges, dams, tunnels and metro lines. Compagnie Generale des Eaux took control in 1984 and the firm merged into SGE in 1988; SGE became VINCI in 2000.

sources.title: Campenon Bernard
sources.publisher: Structurae (International Database for Civil and Structural Engineering)

Electricity Generating Public Company (E.desc: A Thai power holding company set up in 1992 by the state utility EGAT as part of opening electricity generation to private investors; it earns its income from dividends from power plant subsidiaries and joint ventures in Thailand, the Asia-Pacific and North America. It became a public company in 1994 and has traded on the Stock Exchange of Thailand since January 1995.

sources.title: Corporate Profile and History
sources.publisher: Electricity Generating Public Company Limited (EGCO Group)

Lao Holding State Enterprise.desc: A Laotian state-owned company set up in February 2005 to hold the Lao government's shareholdings in power projects, including 25 percent of the Nam Theun 2 Power Company.

EDF (via EDF Nam Theun Holding).desc: France's main electricity company, generating and supplying power with a large nuclear fleet; it had about 120 GW of installed capacity and 41.1 million customers in 2025. The French state completed a buy-out of the shares and became sole shareholder on 26 May 2023; EDF Nam Theun Holding is the group vehicle holding its stake in the Nam Theun 2 project.

sources.title: The French State becomes the sole shareholder of EDF again

Bujagali Energy Limited.desc: A Ugandan independent power producer that owns and runs the 250 MW Bujagali hydropower plant on the Victoria Nile, commissioned in 2012 and supplying up to about 31 percent of Uganda's effective capacity. Its shareholders are TotalEnergies, Bujagali Holdings Power Company (an affiliate of the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development) and the Government of Uganda.

Industrial Promotion Services (Aga Khan.desc: The infrastructure and industrial development arm of the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development, an international development agency; it invests in and runs businesses in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and DR Congo among others. Its power assets have included a 288 MW gas plant in Cote d'Ivoire and a 75 MW diesel plant in Kenya.

sources.title: Bujagali Energy Successfully Delivering First 50MW of Clean Energy to the Ugandan Electricity Grid

Sithe Global.desc: A US power plant developer, Sithe Global Power LLC, with a pipeline of about 5,000 MW of projects in the Philippines, India, Africa and the Middle East. Funds managed by the private equity firm Blackstone bought 80 percent in 2005 and raised the holding to 99 percent in 2011.

sources.title: Bujagali Energy Successfully Delivering First 50MW of Clean Energy to the Ugandan Electricity Grid

THDC India Ltd.desc: An Indian state-controlled power company incorporated in July 1988, building and running hydro, thermal, wind and solar plants and a coal mine, with 3,918 MW of installed capacity. Since a 2020 share sale it is 74.5 percent owned by NTPC Limited and 25.5 percent by the Government of Uttar Pradesh.

Freeport-McMoRan.desc: A US copper, gold and molybdenum mining company incorporated in Delaware in 1987 and listed on the New York Stock Exchange as FCX, with headquarters in Phoenix, Arizona. Its main operations are the Grasberg district in Indonesia, Morenci in Arizona and Cerro Verde in Peru.

Thames Water.desc: A British water and wastewater utility that supplies drinking water and treats sewage for about 16 million customers in London and the Thames Valley. Thames Water Limited was incorporated on 1 April 1989 and is registered in Reading, England.

Voith.desc: A family-owned German technology company based in Heidenheim that makes hydropower plants and equipment, drive systems and papermaking machinery, with almost 21,000 employees.

American Metal Climax (copper subsidiari.desc: A US mining, metals and energy company based in New York, formed in 1957 by merging American Metal Company (founded 1887) with Climax Molybdenum; it later traded as AMAX Inc. Its African copper interests were the Roan Antelope and Mufulira mines, held partly through Rhodesian (later Roan) Selection Trust, of which Zambia took 51 percent in 1970.

KN Construction Company (KNCC).desc: An Indian civil construction contractor described by Human Rights Watch as a regular and major contractor to the state power company NTPC, doing work such as ash dike construction at its Singrauli complex in the 1990s.

sources.title: Memorandum on human rights abuses at NTPC's Singrauli power projects

AES Nile Power.desc: A Ugandan project subsidiary of the US independent power producer AES Corporation of Arlington, Virginia, set up to build, own and operate a 200 MW hydropower station at Bujagali costing about 580 million US dollars. AES withdrew from the project in August 2003 and wrote off about 75 million dollars.

sources.title: Update: AES pulls out of $580 million Uganda dam project

Fortis Bank.desc: The Belgian banking arm of the Fortis financial group. It reported a loss of 20.6 billion euros for 2008; the Belgian state took it over in the 2008 bailout and then sold a 75 percent stake to the French group BNP Paribas, after which it traded as BNP Paribas Fortis.

sources.title: Fortis Bank reveals EUR 20.6bn loss for 2008

Tchad Oil Transportation Company (TOTCO).desc: A pipeline company that runs the 178 km Chadian section of the Chad-Cameroon oil export pipeline. It was formerly an ExxonMobil-led venture; Savannah Energy bought the ExxonMobil interests, and the Chadian state then used a pre-emption right to take TOTCO into state ownership (reported 2023).

sources.title: Chad upset over irregularities in management of pipeline with Cameroon

Coastal Gujarat Power Limited (CGPL).desc: An Indian power company, wholly owned by Tata Power, that built and ran the supercritical coal-fired plant at Mundra, Gujarat (reported at 4,000-4,150 MW). The National Company Law Tribunal approved its merger into Tata Power by an order dated 31 March 2022.

sources.title: NCLT approves amalgamation of Coastal Gujarat Power with Tata Power

Tata Power.desc: An Indian electricity company in the Tata group that generates, transmits and distributes power, including coal, hydro, solar and wind plants. Its total income was 669.92 billion rupees in the 2024-25 financial year.

sources.title: Tata Power reports profit of Rs 47.75 billion in 2024-25

Oyu Tolgoi LLC.desc: The Mongolian company that owns and operates the Oyu Tolgoi copper and gold mine in Umnugovi province, with open-pit mining from 2011 and underground production from March 2023. Rio Tinto holds 66 percent and the Government of Mongolia 34 percent, and the mine is expected to produce up to 500,000 tonnes of copper a year between 2028 and 2036.

Turquoise Hill Resources.desc: A Canadian mining company that held the majority stake in Oyu Tolgoi LLC, with shares listed on the Toronto and New York stock exchanges as TRQ. Rio Tinto bought out the minority shareholders for about 3.1 billion US dollars and completed the takeover on 15 December 2022, making it a wholly owned Rio Tinto subsidiary.

sources.title: Rio Tinto completes acquisition of Turquoise Hill

Erdenes Oyu Tolgoi LLC.desc: A Mongolian state-owned company, a wholly owned subsidiary of the state holding company Erdenes Mongol LLC, set up in 2011 to hold the government's 34 percent shareholding in Oyu Tolgoi LLC.

Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinée (CBG).desc: A Guinean bauxite mining company running the Sangaredi mine and the rail and port works at Kamsar, holding exclusive bauxite rights in north-western Guinea. The Government of Guinea holds 49 percent and Halco Mining 51 percent; the mine produced 13.7 million tonnes of bauxite in 2019.

Halco Mining Inc..desc: A holding company that owns 51 percent of Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinee; it is a joint venture of the mining groups Rio Tinto and Alcoa and the privately owned Dadco group.

Alcoa.desc: A US aluminium company incorporated in Delaware that mines bauxite, refines alumina and smelts and casts aluminium, with 26 operating sites in nine countries. Its shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange, and it had about 13,900 employees at the end of 2024.

sources.title: Alcoa Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal year 2024

Dadco.desc: A privately owned investment, manufacturing and trading group with roots in the aluminium industry going back to a founding company of 1915, supplying smelter-grade alumina and alumina chemicals in Europe. Its head office is in Guernsey with a sales office in Lausanne, and its Aluminium Oxid Stade refinery in Germany can make over one million tonnes of alumina a year; it is a shareholder in Halco Mining.

Mota-Engil Engenharia e Construção Áfric.desc: The African construction arm of Mota-Engil, a Portuguese engineering and construction group with about 70 years in the business and operations in 24 countries, 15 of them in Africa, including Uganda. The parent company's shares trade in Lisbon under the ticker EGL.

RANSA.desc: A Peruvian logistics company, Ransa Comercial S.A.C., based in Callao, founded in 1939 as a cotton storage business and now running warehousing, customs bonded and cold storage, cargo handling and road transport, including hazardous materials. It has more than 7,000 employees, and the private equity firm H.I.G. Capital became majority shareholder of Grupo Ransa in 2021.

sources.title: Ransa Comercial S.A.C. pre-operational certification audit report

Montana Exploradora de Guatemala.desc: A Guatemalan gold and silver mining company, dating from 1996, that ran the Marlin mine in San Marcos from 2005; the mine produced 202,200 ounces of gold in 2013 and stopped producing on 31 May 2017. It was a wholly owned subsidiary of Glamis Gold, which merged into the Canadian miner Goldcorp in 2006.

sources.title: Goldcorp's Marlin mine: a decade of operations and controversy in Guatemala
Montana Exploradora de Guatemala, S.A. (1996-present)
sources.publisher: Legal Cultures of the Subsoil, Institute of Latin American Studies, University of London

Nachtigal Hydropower Company (NHPC).desc: A Cameroonian project company that owns and operates the 420 MW Nachtigal hydropower plant on the Sanaga river, built for about 1.2 billion euros under a 35-year concession. At the 2018 signing its shareholders were EDF (40 percent), the IFC (30 percent) and the Republic of Cameroon (30 percent).

sources.title: EDF, IFC and the Republic of Cameroon sign final and binding agreements for the construction of the Nachtigal hydroelectric dam in Cameroon
EDF, IFC, Republic of Cameroon sign agreements to build 420-MW Nachtigal hydropower plant

Desarrollos Energéticos S.A. (DESA).desc: A Honduran hydropower developer behind the Agua Zarca project, planned at 21.3 MW with about 98.8 GWh a year. Its executive president, Roberto David Castillo Mejia, was arrested in 2018 over the murder of Berta Caceres.

sources.title: Desarrollos Energeticos executive arrested in murder of anti-hydro activist in Honduras

Empresa Eléctrica Pangue S.A..desc: A Chilean electricity company set up for the Pangue hydroelectric project on the upper Biobio river. The International Finance Corporation held 2.5 percent of its equity and lent it 170 million US dollars from October 1993, selling the stake in July 2002.

sources.title: Chile: Empresa Electrica Pangue S.A.-01 / Upper Bio-Bio Watershed

Hidroeléctrica Santa Rita S.A..desc: A Guatemalan company formed to build the 23 MW Santa Rita hydroelectric plant on the Rio Icbolay in Alta Verapaz, registered as the project participant for a UN Clean Development Mechanism project. It was part-owned by the Latin Renewables Infrastructure Fund, which later said it would not develop the project.

sources.title: Guatemala: Investigation of Indigenous Peoples Concerns Regarding Hydropower Project
Santa Rita Hydroelectric Plant, CDM project record
sources.publisher: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change

Real Infrastructure Capital Partners.desc: A private equity fund manager that sponsors the Latin Renewables Infrastructure Fund, which invests in renewable energy projects in Latin America. The fund reached a first close of about 50 million US dollars in 2012 against a target of 150 to 200 million.

sources.title: Real Infrastructure Capital Partners Reaches First Close for Latin Renewables Infrastructure Fund

PT Asiatic Persada.desc: An Indonesian oil palm plantation company in Jambi, Sumatra, holding a 20,000-hectare permit granted in 1986. The Singapore-listed agribusiness group Wilmar International took control in 2006 and sold it in April 2013 to Prima Fortune International and PT Agro Mandiri Semesta.

sources.title: Palm oil deal undermines efforts to resolve 25-year conflict in Sumatra

PT Agro Mandiri Semesta (Ganda Group).desc: An Indonesian oil palm company and a unit of the Ganda Group, owned by Ganda Sitorus, brother of Wilmar International's founder Martua Sitorus.

sources.title: Palm oil deal undermines efforts to resolve 25-year conflict in Sumatra

Oil Palm Uganda Ltd (OPUL).desc: A Ugandan oil palm plantation company that signed an agreement with the Ugandan government in 2003 to run an integrated palm oil project in Kalangala district, part of the state Vegetable Oil Development Project backed by IFAD and the World Bank. It sits within the Bidco Uganda venture, licensed in September 2003 for a planned 30,000-hectare plantation across Kalangala and Masaka.

Bidco Oil Refineries.desc: A family-run Kenyan manufacturer of edible oils, fats, soaps and personal care goods, founded by the Shah family with a soap factory at Thika in 1985 and now trading as Bidco Africa, with over 40 brands sold in 16 African countries. Annual turnover was reported above 500 million US dollars in 2013.

sources.title: Be persistent, never give up: The story of Vimal Shah and Bidco
sources.publisher: How we made it in Africa

EDF International (Électricité de France.desc: A wholly owned subsidiary of the French electricity group EDF that holds and manages the group's investments in energy companies outside France, including EDF Energy, Edison, Luminus and EDF Inc. The net book value of its shareholdings was 23.3 billion euros at the end of 2022.

Grupo GOLAN.note: Searched for Grupo Golan / Golan Group in connection with Guatemala and the Marlin mine; the only page found that described the firm was SourceWatch, a user-edited wiki, which the brief rules out as a sole source. The Amnesty International report on the Marlin mine, which I opened, does not name it. No company site, register entry or news report describing the firm could be opened.

Ruhore Company Limited.note: Searched for Ruhore Company Limited (Uganda, Soroti quarry, Mota-Engil subcontractor). No company website, Uganda Registration Services Bureau entry or news report naming the firm could be found or opened; the Daily Monitor article on the Tororo-Kamdini quarry disputes that I opened describes an unnamed company and does not identify Ruhore.

Siemens.desc: A German technology company founded in Berlin in 1847, making automation, digitalisation and electrification equipment and software for industry, buildings, power grids and transport. Group revenue was 78.9 billion euros in the 2025 financial year.

sources.title: Earnings Release and Financial Results Q4 FY 2025

Industrial and Commercial Bank of China.desc: A Chinese state-controlled commercial bank, founded in 1984, offering lending, deposits and other banking services; its A-shares trade in Shanghai and H-shares in Hong Kong since its 2006 listing. It had nearly 49 trillion yuan of total assets and about 170 million personal customers at the end of 2024.

sources.title: 2024 Annual Results Presentation
sources.publisher: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

Hoang Anh Gia Lai (HAGL).desc: A Vietnamese agriculture company whose main businesses are fruit, mostly bananas and durians for export, and pig farming; it is chaired by Doan Nguyen Duc and listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange. Net revenue was 5,694 billion dong (about 227 million US dollars) in 2024.

sources.title: Vietnam's agri major Hoang Anh Gia Lai sees profit down 41% in 2024

Dragon Capital Group.desc: An independent investment and asset management firm founded in Ho Chi Minh City in 1994, managing listed equity, fixed income, clean technology and property funds focused on Vietnam, with offices in Hanoi, Hong Kong, Bangkok and Bath. It launched the Vietnam Enterprise Investments Limited (VEIL) fund in 1995 and listed it on the London Stock Exchange main market in 2016.

Vitens.desc: A Dutch drinking water company that abstracts groundwater, treats it at 93 production sites and distributes it through about 48,000 km of mains to around 6 million people and businesses across five provinces. It delivered 352.9 million cubic metres of water and had 1,910 permanent staff in 2025, and is owned by government bodies as shareholders.

Rand Water.desc: A South African water board established under the Water Services Act of 1997 and classified as a national government business enterprise, selling bulk drinking water to municipalities, mines and industry in Gauteng and parts of neighbouring provinces. Its shareholder is the national government through the Minister of Water and Sanitation; it supplied an average of 4,642 megalitres a day and employed 3,437 staff in 2021-22.

sources.title: Integrated Annual Report 2021/22
sources.publisher: Rand Water (tabled in the South African Parliament)

China State Construction Engineering Cor.desc: A Chinese state-owned investment and construction group founded in 1982 and based in Beijing, working on housing, infrastructure, property development and design in China and abroad. It reported revenue of about 290 billion US dollars and 370,272 employees, ranking 17th on the Fortune Global 500.

sources.title: China State Construction Engineering, Global 500 profile

Societe Zhengwei Technique Cooperation S.desc: A Chinese-owned construction company operating in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where it has taken government contracts for road works and, in 2020, for drilling water boreholes in five provinces with the Belgian firm Putman-Malcon&TSE.

sources.title: DRC: SZTC and Putman-Malcon&TSE to drill 28 water wells in Grand Kasai

China Railway Seventh Group (CRSG).desc: A Chinese state-held construction company, part of China Railway Group Limited and founded by China Railway Engineering Corporation, which builds roads, railways, bridges, tunnels, buildings and hydroelectric works and makes concrete components.

sources.title: China Railway Seventh (7th) Group Co. Ltd (CRSG) organisation profile

Cairo Electricity Production Company (CE.desc: An Egyptian state electricity generator, a subsidiary of the Egyptian Electricity Holding Company, which owns and operates power stations around Cairo including the 1,500 MW Giza North combined-cycle gas plant built with a 600 million US dollar World Bank loan.
